fields.h1: Build a White Elephant Sign-Up Sheet That Assigns Draw Numbers
fields.hero_description: Build a white elephant sign up sheet that counts who is playing, confirms the price limit, and hands out draw numbers.
fields.features_heading: Settled Before the First Gift Is Opened
fields.features_subheading: The sheet decides who plays, what each gift costs, and who picks first. Describe your exchange, and Emergent builds it.
fields.feature_1:
Players counted apart from watchers

Asks each guest whether they are bringing a gift and playing, or coming to watch. The host sees two totals and knows how many wrapped gifts should be on the table that night.
fields.feature_2:
The price limit, agreed on the form

Shows the spending limit right above the gift question and asks every player to tick that they agree. A $60 speaker never ends up in a pile where every other gift cost $25.
fields.feature_3:
Draw numbers dealt when sign-ups close

Gives each player a random number the moment the sheet closes and emails it to them. Number 1 opens the first gift, and the order is fixed before anyone walks in the door.
fields.feature_4:
A separate round for kids or teams

Asks one sorting question, such as age or department, and sends each answer to its own round with its own limit. Kids swap $10 gifts while the adult round plays for $30.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders for gifts still missing

Emails any player who has not added a gift by the date you choose, a few days before the party. Nobody has to send the group chat a reminder and wait to see who answers.
fields.feature_6:
Your guest list, your code

Keeps every sign-up in a database you own, so next year's invites start from this year's player list. On paid plans, export the app's full code to your GitHub repository.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Hosts Ran Their Sign-Ups
fields.tab_content_1:
Each of 22 players owes one gift, the 6 watchers none

Clotilde Penhaligon runs the Brackenhurst Freight holiday exchange with a $25 limit. The sheet first asks each coworker: playing, or only watching? By the close, 28 people have signed up: 22 playing, 6 watching. Euphemia Tregunna is a watcher. Clotilde gets both totals by email and plans for 22 gifts.
fields.tab_content_2:
Ptolemy is 9, which puts him in the $10 kids' round

Wendeline Treadgold hosts her family's exchange, and the sheet asks each guest's age. Anyone under 12 goes to a kids' round with a $10 limit, and adults play for $30. Ptolemy Treadgold is 9 and lands with the kids. Of 18 guests, 11 are adults and 7 are kids, and each round opens gifts from its own pile.
fields.tab_content_3:
An email for each of the 3 missing gifts

Albertine Kestermoor runs the Greyhallow Studio exchange on a video call for a team with no office. Each of the 14 players adds a link to a gift bought online. Links stay hidden until the call, and the buyer ships each gift to whoever keeps it. Three days out, 11 links are in, and the 3 players without one get an email reminder.
fields.tab_content_4:
Every one of 30 players gets a draw number

Brennagh Radcliffe caps the Haverleigh Road Fellowship sheet at 30 players, one per folding chair. When spot 30 fills, the sheet closes and the app emails every player a random draw number. Philomena Quarrie draws 17. Anyone who signs up later goes on a waitlist and gets a number if a player drops out.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a White Elephant Sign-Up Sheet
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to make a white elephant sign up sheet that counts players, holds the price limit, and sets the draw order.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Settle the limit before anything else
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask whether each guest is playing
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Choose a close date and a cap
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Decide how the draw order is set
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick one price limit, such as $25, and put it in both the invitation and the form. A single number leaves less room for argument than a range does. Add a theme, like gifts under a pound or regifts only, if the group wants one.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Some guests want the party without buying a gift. Make playing or watching the first question, and ask watchers nothing more. Your count of players is your count of gifts, and it also tells you how long the game will run.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Close sign-ups two or three days before the party, which leaves time for reminders and late shopping. If the room or the clock limits you, cap the number of players and send anyone past the cap to a waitlist.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Random numbers given out at the close keep the order out of anyone's hands. Email each player their number and keep the full list for the host, who calls number 1 first. A player who drops out frees a number for the waitlist.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Add a round for kids or a team
fields.howto_step_5_des: If children or separate teams take part, ask one question that sorts them, such as age, and give each round its own limit and its own pile of gifts. Keep that question short, because the answer decides where every gift goes.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Write one prompt that covers the limit and the questions, then the close date and how numbers go out. Emergent turns that prompt into a working sheet with its own player list. To change the cap or a question later, prompt again in plain English.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Enter four test sign-ups, one of them a watcher and one past the cap. Check that the totals count only players and that the extra sign-up lands on the waitlist. Each test player should get a number by email. Delete the test rows before sharing.

faq_plan.q: What is a white elephant sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: A white elephant sign up sheet is the list of people joining a gift exchange. Each entry holds a name, whether that person is bringing a gift and playing, and their agreement to the price limit. The host reads it to count gifts and to set who picks first.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a white elephant sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: Write one prompt for Emergent's AI form builder that names the price limit, the questions to ask, when sign-ups close, and how draw numbers go out. Emergent builds the form and the database behind it. Share the link with guests and watch the list fill.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a white elephant sign up sheet have?
faq_plan.a: Four is enough: a name, playing or watching, a tick agreeing to the price limit, and an email address for the draw number. Leave out sizes and wish lists unless the game needs them. Each extra question is one more reason for a guest to put off signing up.

faq_plan.q: How do I set the price limit on a white elephant sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: Write the limit into the gift question itself, for example: bring one wrapped gift worth up to $25. Then require a tick next to it before the form submits. Repeat the same number in the confirmation email, and the limit is in writing twice before anyone shops.

faq_plan.q: How many players does a white elephant sign up sheet need?
faq_plan.a: Aim for at least 8 players, which gives each gift a few chances to be stolen. At the top end, a turn takes a minute or two, and 30 players fill about an hour. Emergent puts no response cap on the form, and the only cap is the one you choose.

faq_plan.q: How do draw numbers work on a white elephant sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: When sign-ups close, the app shuffles the player list and gives each player one number. Number 1 opens a gift first, and every later number either unwraps a new gift or steals an opened one. Emergent builds the shuffle and the emails from one line in your prompt.

faq_plan.q: Can a white elephant sign up sheet work for a remote team?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Instead of a wrapped box, each player adds a gift link and a one-line teaser, and the host reads the teasers aloud on the call. Steals work the same way on screen. Ask for a mailing address only from the player who keeps each gift, once the game ends.

faq_plan.q: Can I add a potluck to a white elephant sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add a second section after the gift questions that asks what each guest is bringing to eat, grouped by course. Watchers can bring a dish even when they skip the gift. For a dinner with no gift exchange, a potluck sign up sheet is the simpler build.

faq_plan.q: Should a white elephant sign up sheet include a gift theme?
faq_plan.a: Only if the group agrees on one. A theme such as regifts only or something homemade narrows the shopping and gives the pile a shared joke. Put it beside the price limit on the form with one short example of a gift that fits.

faq_plan.q: Can I reuse a white elephant sign up sheet next year?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Keep the link, clear the old entries, and change the date and the limit before sending it out again. Read last year's watchers first: a few of them may want to play this time, and a personal invitation is a good way to ask.

plan.angle: The top 10 for white elephant sign up sheet is printable grids, Etsy PDFs and number cards: a sheet a host fills by hand and still has to count, police and shuffle. This page shows the sheet as a phone form that does that work: an office party that counts players apart from watchers, a family exchange that routes kids under 12 to their own $10 round, a remote team that gets a reminder when a gift is missing 3 days before the call, and a fellowship hall whose 30 spots close and hand out random draw numbers. The FAQ covers what to ask, the price limit, player counts, draw numbers, remote play, potluck add-ons, close dates and reuse.
